hero.heading: The Stay Different|Colour Guide
hero.sub: Find the shade that does not just match you — it feels like you.

opening.heading: Your shade|starts here
opening.body:
The right colour does more than look good in a photo. It warms your complexion, brightens your eyes and makes people ask what you have changed.

Three things point you in the right direction: your skin tone (how light or deep you are), your undertone (the colour beneath the surface) and contrast (how much your hair stands apart from your skin).

Consider this a guide, not a rulebook. The best shade is the one you feel most like yourself in — and if that breaks every rule here, even better.

pillars.title: Skin tone
pillars.text: How light or deep your skin is on the surface. It changes with the seasons.

pillars.title: Undertone
pillars.text: The warm, cool or neutral colour underneath. It never changes.

pillars.title: Contrast
pillars.text: How far your hair sits from your skin. Low blends, high makes a statement.

step1.heading: Know your|undertone
step1.body: Skin tone is the shade you see in the mirror — fair, medium, deep. Undertone is the subtle hue underneath it, and it stays the same whether you are winter-pale or holiday-bronzed. It is the secret to a shade that looks expensive instead of off.
step1.quizIntro: Three quick questions. Go with your first instinct.

quiz.question: Look at the veins on your inner wrist in daylight. What colour are they?
Which jewellery makes your skin glow?
How does your skin react to the sun?

options.label: I tan easily and rarely burn
I burn first, tan later (if at all)

undertones.name: Warm
undertones.description: Your skin has golden, peachy or yellow hints underneath. You glow in sunlight and look radiant in earthy, rich colours.

undertones.name: Cool
undertones.description: Your skin has pink, red or bluish hints underneath. You shine in jewel tones and crisp colours, and warmth can sometimes make you look flushed.

undertones.name: Neutral
undertones.description: A balance of warm and cool — your undertone is hard to pin down, and that is your superpower. Almost every shade family works for you.

step2.heading: Find|your shade
step2.body: Seven shades, each with its own personality. Filter by undertone or how much dimension you want, then fall in love.

texture.heading: Colour looks different|on curls
texture.body: Curls and coils catch light differently to straight hair, so dimension reads deeper and highlights pop harder. These two were made for it.

step3.heading: Choose by|the look
step3.body: Know the vibe but not the shade name? Start with how you want to feel.

looks.statement: I want rich brunette with a hint of warmth
I want bold highlights on my curls
I want to change the room when I walk in

step4.heading: Harmony|or contrast?
step4.body: Once you know your undertone, decide how loud you want to be. There is no wrong answer — only a different one.

harmony.label: Harmony
harmony.title: Blend in beautifully
harmony.text: Match your hair to your undertone — warm with warm, cool with cool. The result is seamless, soft and naturally "is that your real hair?"
harmony.example: Warm undertone + Cocoa Muse · Cool undertone + Smoke Signal

contrast.label: Contrast
contrast.title: Stand out on purpose
contrast.text: Pair opposites — cool skin with golden warmth, deep skin with bright blonde — and turn your hair into the statement. Contrast is not a mistake. It is a choice.
contrast.example: Deep skin + Golden Hour · Cool undertone + Wild Card

closing.heading: Your hair. Your rules.|Stay different.
closing.body: Lighting, screens and your own natural hair all change how a colour looks in real life. Use this guide to narrow it down, then choose the shade that feels most like you. Still torn? We will happily help you decide.
